description: The bar chart illustrates the perplexity values for two different methods across a series of percentage categories. The horizontal axis contains the categories, which are percentages ordered ascendingly from 10% to 80% in 10% increments, without an explicit axis label. The vertical axis represents the value and is labeled "Perplexity," utilizing a logarithmic scale with major tick marks at $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$, accompanied by horizontal dashed grid lines at these intervals. The chart features grouped bars, with two bars presented side-by-side for each percentage category. According to the legend in the top left corner, the blue bars represent the "Per-Output" method and the orange bars represent the "Per-Layer" method. The values for both methods start low and increase as the percentage categories increase. The shortest bars are located at the 10% category, where both the blue and orange bars have approximate values of 5 to 6, remaining below the $10^1$ mark. The values stay relatively stable up to the 50% category, after which they begin to rise more noticeably. The tallest bars are found at the 80% category, where the blue "Per-Output" bar reaches approximately 500 and the orange "Per-Layer" bar reaches approximately 900, just below the $10^3$ mark. The categories are sorted in ascending numerical order, and there is a visual emphasis in the form of a solid gray shaded rectangle placed below the horizontal axis, spanning the area between the 40% and 50% category labels.
